M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

scenario_results.name: default_init_up_to_f3_via_f2

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies F1 PS3 direct upward motion to MU3, arrival at F3, then PS2 request downward to MD2 and arrival at F2.
scenario_results.name: default_init_direct_to_f3_then_down_to_f2

scenario_results.name: hot_start_f2_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start from reachable F3 verifies PS1 chooses downward MD1 and S1 arrival stops at F1.
scenario_results.name: hot_start_f3_down_to_f1

scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_motion

scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_floor

scenario_results.name: reset_forces_f1_from_down_motion

scenario_results.name: no_event_holds_current_floor

evidence: NL names floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL specifies F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL contains these transitions.
NL specifies MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL contains these transitions.
NL says reset forces controller back to floor 1; DSL has forced transition `! * -> F1 :: Reset`.
NL says hbrg distinguishes upward, downward, and stop conditions; DSL sets hbrg=1 in MU states, -1 in MD states, and 0 in floor states.
findings.summary: The DSL is broadly faithful to the NL: it includes all named floor and motion states, the specified request-triggered departures, arrival-sensor completions, reset-to-F1 behavior, and hbrg stop/up/down output assignments.

evidence: GroundingMap marks all required states, events, transitions, hbrg actions, initial transition, and reset transition as required and mapped to NL evidence.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 11 normal transitions, 7 forced reset transitions, 7 events, 1 variable, and 7 actions.
sim_summary reports 8/8 scenarios passing, including upward travel, downward travel, arrival stopping, reset from motion/floor contexts, and no-event hold behavior.
findings.summary: Core component coverage is strong for the stated finite-state elevator abstraction: states, events, transitions, reset, and output actions are all represented and grounded.

evidence: NL says the controller 'immediately checks the next destination before deciding whether to continue moving' and reset acts 'regardless of the outstanding request context'.
DSL has no request-memory variables or queue/context state; floor requests are modeled only as events consumed at floor states, and motion states ignore PS1/PS2/PS3.
The explicit NL transition list does not require queueing or same-floor PS self-transitions, so this is not assessed as a blocking fidelity defect.
findings.summary: The model does not explicitly encode persistent outstanding request context or same-floor request handling; this is likely acceptable for the explicit transition list but is a residual interpretation risk from the NL wording about checking the next destination and reset regardless of outstanding request context.

findings.summary: The five-component summary is empty, reducing review triangulation, although the NL, DSL, GroundingMap, diagnostics, and simulations provide enough evidence for a safe pass decision.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary reports advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR: Variable 'hbrg' does not affect any transition guard.
NL defines hbrg as an output distinguishing upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
DSL uses hbrg only in enter actions, which is appropriate for an output indicator.
findings.summary: The W_UNREFERENCED_VAR warning for hbrg should not be treated as requiring a guard-based repair because hbrg is an output variable, not control logic.

evidence: All required GroundingMap elements have corresponding DSL constructs.
design_diagnostics_summary ok=true with blocking_count=0 and one advisory warning.
sim_summary ok=true with 8 scenarios passed out of 8.
The remaining risks are interpretive edge cases rather than missing required core structure.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate. No quality cap is warranted because the model is not an empty shell, required states/transitions/actions are present, diagnostics are non-blocking, and scenario evidence exercises the principal behavior.
